topic:
Reference evidence for the OpenBot parity build of skilled bots.

Inputs, all read-only. Do not edit any of them.
- The ten reference repos under specs/system-skilled-bots/context/: OpenBot-main (the primary reference), OpenMausBot-main, rakazo-main, openhuman-main, openhuman-full, OpenGhost-main, hermes-muse-main, turnstone-main, buzz-main and tinychannels-main.
- The build plan: the fourteen phase folders and the contracts/ folder of specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build (001-activity-and-actor, 002-routine-layer, 003-terminal-screen, 004-computer-exposure, 005-memory, 006-approval-grants, 007-per-bot-apps, 008-vault, 009-skills, 010-conversations, 011-messaging-channels, 012-manual-testing-scenarios, 013-skilled-and-doc-alignment, 014-deep-review).
- The three earlier syntheses: specs/system-skilled-bots/002-openbot-parity-research/001-openbot-parity-research/research/research.md, .../002-plan-review-research/research/research.md and .../003-plan-depth-research/research/research.md.
- The built runtime: .skilled/skills/system-skilled-bots/runtime/lib/, .skilled/bin/bots.cjs and .skilled/skills/system-skilled-bots/scripts/bot-check.cjs.

Answer two things.

1. Evidence per planned phase. For each of the fourteen phases: which reference files and lines implement the same thing; what a builder should lift or mirror, with the licence of the source; where the plan differs from how the references do it, and which side the evidence supports; and which failures, tests and fixes in those repos the plan does not yet guard against.

2. Net-new. What do the ten repos have that neither the build plan nor the skip list in section 13 of the parity synthesis covers? Rank each by its value to a small team and give its size. Read openhuman-full first: no earlier run studied it, and it carries five vendored crates (tinyagents, tinyconnectors, tinymemory, tinyhumans-sdk, tinysecurity) and a built openhuman-tui crate that openhuman-main lacks.

Rules.
- Do not repeat a finding one of the three earlier syntheses already carries. Cite the earlier finding and add only what is new.
- Cite every claim as [SOURCE: path:line]. A claim with no resolving citation is not a finding.
- Mark each claim observed (you read the line) or inferred (you reason from it).
- Name the 003 phase every finding belongs to. A finding that fits no phase goes under net-new.
- Write only inside your own lineage folder.

noveltyJustification: 8 findings: 6 fully new to the packet (panic-safe restore, bounded preview marker, render-loop coalescing, tinysecurity approval engine, reply-intent parser, tinymemory namespaces) and 2 that add a new divergence against a citation the plan already holds.

focus: 006-approval-grants, 007-per-bot-apps and 008-vault: what the tinysecurity approval engine, policy default and redaction rule set do that the plan's kind-first ladder, item-id answer and value-based leak matcher do not
noveltyJustification: 5 findings: 4 are fully new to the packet (origin rung before the kind rung, instance-and-generation answer binding, validator-based redaction, JSON-escaped and unbounded post-run scan) and 1 is a new net-new candidate (owner-shell command scan).

focus: 011-messaging-channels and 002-routine-layer: what tinychannels delivers on durability negotiation and conformance fixtures, and what OpenBot's firing frame and routine checklist fix that the plan's four-part routine block does not guard
noveltyJustification: 5 findings: 4 fully new (firing frame after a silent no-op success, bounded routine checklist, durability negotiation, conformance-kit prohibition) and 1 negative ranking of provider breadth.

focus: 005-memory and 004-computer-exposure: turnstone's stable memory identity and body-free index, OpenGhost's crowded-mark compaction, and the pinned prompt block the plan does not refresh on resume
noveltyJustification: 5 findings: 3 fully new (stable identity versus positional index, crowded-mark compaction, pinned memory block on resume), 1 new test-corpus pattern, and 1 negative confirmation for 004.

focus: Net-new sweep over OpenBot-main/shared: six ranked candidates for a later packet plus the optimistic-row rule 001 already satisfies by construction
noveltyJustification: 7 findings: 6 fully new net-new candidates (what-if explainer, orchestration threads, attachments, connect-prompt, tool wording, client-side redaction warning) and 1 confirmation with a named failure rule for 001.

focus: 003-terminal-screen child 005-answer-flow and 010-conversations: the command-preview sanitizer exception, the approval card as a diff, the paste guard, and the display-copy rule turnstone states
noveltyJustification: 5 findings: 3 fully new (command preview keeps control characters, approval card as a diff, paste never sends) plus one rule and one negative finding confirming the plan's chat contract.

focus: 012-manual-testing-scenarios, 013-skilled-and-doc-alignment and 014-deep-review: the artifact shapes in openhuman-full that the plan rules do not cover, from a sigpipe test to a findings note that records its rejected hypothesis
noveltyJustification: 5 findings all fully new: three test-corpus patterns the 33-scenario table lacks, an agent-facing doc index, and the review-note shape with rejected hypothesis and correction.

focus: Second net-new sweep over the remaining twenty-one vendored crates, which yields two guards a planned phase needs (tinyskills supply-chain scan for 009, tinyeventqueues inbound dispositions for 011) and a licence-closed ranking of the rest
noveltyJustification: 5 findings all fully new: the skill-body supply-chain scan, the skill-set procedural guards, the inbound disposition ledger, two aggregate test properties, and the ranking of ten crates under a GPL-3.0-only licence.

focus: 007-per-bot-apps: the reference tool-call gate (a five-step privilege ladder, a caller maximum, a cron read-only ceiling, an hourly budget and a payload-free typed denial) against the plan server-list filter
noveltyJustification: 5 findings: 4 fully new (permission ladder and caller maximum, cron read-only ceiling, pre-prompt hourly budget, payload-free denial for the model) and 1 inferred high-value net-new candidate combining them.

focus: Consolidation: per-phase coverage across the 50 findings, the licence wall across all ten repos, one merged net-new ranking, the three questions the corpus cannot answer, and the three recurring failure classes
noveltyJustification: 5 findings of synthesis rather than discovery: coverage counts, the licence filter, the merged ranking, three unanswerable questions and three failure classes, each derived from this lineage's own findings.
